place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 山门外的林子
place.en: Chending Temple · the woods outside the gate

setup.zh: 三试，胆子：林子里一只蠪侄，九首九尾，虎爪，叫声像婴儿，拴在古松上。一半的孩子哭着跑了。石蛋排在你后头：「我跟着你走。」
setup.en: Third trial, nerve: in the woods a Longzhi — nine heads, nine tails, tiger claws, a cry like an infant's — chained to an old pine. Half the children run away crying. Shidan is queued behind you: "I'll follow you."

recap.zh: 三试，胆子：你听出了蠪侄的真头。一颗石子打中它的后腿，铁桩连泥拔起半尺，链子长出一截；木牌一烫——「……左边」。你往右一滚，那一爪落在了你身后的石蛋身上。名册上写的是「林中自失」。
recap.en: Third trial, nerve: you heard the Longzhi's true head. A pebble struck its hind leg, the stake tore half a foot out of the mud and the chain ran a length longer; the token burned — "…Left." You rolled right, and the claw fell on Shidan behind you. The register says "lost himself in the forest".

zh: 九首，九尾，虎爪；其音如婴儿。
锁链够不着的地方，站着两个人。铁桩埋在泥里，是松的。
en: Nine heads, nine tails, tiger claws; a voice like an infant.
Just beyond the chain's reach, two people stand. The stake in the mud is loose.

story.zh:
二试下来，剩了不到三百人。马小宝的考牌上是一个圈。马三在山门外头，把那封信又亮了一亮，执事看看信，朝正殿那边望了一眼，没有说话，放他进了队——怎么补，执事说了算。

三试考胆子，在山门外西边的一片老林子里。林子里的树，一棵比一棵老，一棵比一棵黑，大白天走进去，也像走进了傍晚。林子正中是一棵古松，松树底下，拿一根比人腿还粗的铁链，拴着一只妖兽：身子像狐狸，却比牛还大；九个脑袋，九条尾巴，四只爪子是虎的爪子。九个脑袋一齐转过来，盯着每一个走进林子的孩子；九张嘴一齐张开，叫起来像九个婴儿在同时哭，哭声在林子里撞来撞去，撞得人头皮发麻，脚底发软。

守林子的是另一个执事，站在林子口，道：「里头拴的是一只蠪侄，拴了几十年了。进去，走到古松底下，摸一下松树皮，出来，画一道。一个一个进。」头一个进去的孩子，走了不到十步，便哭着跑了出来。第二个走了五步。第三个站在林子口，腿抖了半天，一步也没迈进去，给他爹从人群里拽走了。

排队的时候，有个穿绸衫的孩子，家里请过先生，这时候见大家都怕，便要显一显本事，摇头晃脑地背起《山海经》来：「有兽焉，其状如狐，而九尾、九首、虎爪，名曰蠪侄，其音如婴儿——」背到这里，他顿住了。旁边一个孩子问：「其音如婴儿，然后呢？」那穿绸衫的孩子脸色慢慢地白了，嘴唇哆嗦了两下，才把最后三个字挤出来：「……是、食、人。」四下里登时一片死寂。过了一会儿，不知是谁先「哇」的一声哭了出来，跟着便哭成了一片。

马小宝进去了。他走了三步。第三步落地的时候，蠪侄的九个脑袋一齐转向了他。马小宝站住了，一动不动，好一会儿，林子外头的人都瞧见，他那条绸裤子的裤腿底下，慢慢地洇开了一滩水。两个家丁冲进林子，一左一右把他抬了出来。马小宝给抬在半空里，两条腿乱蹬，嘴里还在喊：「我没有！是露水！是露水！」林子外头的人，这一回谁也憋不住了，「哈哈哈哈」笑得东倒西歪，有的抱着肚子蹲在地上，有的笑得直拍旁人的后背。只有一个人没有笑，是马三。

马三却没有走。他站在人堆里，眼睛从儿子湿了的裤子上挪开，一寸一寸地挪，挪到了排在队尾的小满身上。他招手叫过葛六，低声说了几句。葛六的脸色变了一变，摇了摇头。马三又说了一句，从怀里摸出一锭银子。葛六看了那锭银子很久，没有接。马三的脸沉了下来，道：「那五两，你也别要了。」葛六没说话，退到人堆后头去了，却没有走。马三便把那锭银子塞给了身边一个家丁，又摸出一小块，走到林子口，塞进了守林执事的袖子里。

轮到小满之前，他在林子外头等了将近一个时辰。别的孩子等的时候，有的在哭，有的闭着眼睛念佛。小满什么也没做。他就蹲在林子边上，歪着头，听。他也看见了那个揣银子的家丁：挤在人堆最前头，手在地上摸了一颗石子，掂一掂，又摸一颗，挑了一颗最圆的，攥在手心里，眼睛一直落在他身上。小满心里有了数——那颗石子是冲他来的。进了林子，背冲着人堆站，那颗石子便只能打在他背上。只有一回，他抬了抬眼：阿禾走进了林子，闭着眼睛，一步一步，不快不慢，走到古松底下摸了一把树皮，又闭着眼睛走了出来，从头到尾没看那兽一眼。

石蛋排在他后头，挨着他蹲下了。他的考牌上只有一道，三试过了也凑不满三道，可他还是排着。他小声道：「你算得出来。」小满道：「什么？」石蛋道：「那九个数。你算得出来，你也听得出来。」他把那一双满是老茧的手在膝盖上搓了又搓，「三道凑不满，我也要进去摸一把。摸了，测灵的时候我去跪着求。那个点头的执事，他认得太华山的人。」小满张了张嘴，没说出话来。

他爹教过他，怎么分狼嚎和风声：狼嚎是从胸口里出来的，是热的；风只有一个洞，再响也是空的。他听了一个时辰。那九个脑袋叫一回，他听一回。听到后来，他发觉一桩怪事：每回九张嘴一齐张开，九种哭声一齐涌出来，林子深处那棵古松的松针，只跟着其中一种哭声抖。别的八种，哭得再响，松针一动也不动。

轮到他了。他走进林子，没有往前冲，站在铁链够不着的地方，站定了，闭上了眼睛。九种哭声，一齐涌进他耳朵里来。他一种一种地听。第一种，是空的，像风灌进一只破瓦罐。第二种，也是空的，像有人对着一口枯井喊了一声，井底下应回来的那一声。第三种、第四种、第五种、第六种、第七种，空的。第九种，空的。只有第八种，不是。第八种是从胸腔里出来的，一呼一吸之间，带着热气，带着一股说不出的腥，还带着一点饿。那是一种很深很深的饿，饿得发慌，饿得不管不顾，好像把整座林子吃下去，把整座山吃下去，也不会饱。另外八个，都是它的影子。

他站得太久了。林子口，守林的执事抬头看了看天，日头已经偏西，后头还排着一百多个。他把手一挥：「站着不动算什么？下一个，一块儿进，快些。」石蛋便跟了进来，踩着小满的脚印，一步一步，停在小满身后两步远的地方，小声道：「我跟着你走。」

小满睁开眼睛，弯下腰，从地上捡起了一块石头。
story.en:
After the second trial, fewer than three hundred were left. Ma Xiaobao's tag had a circle on it. Outside the gate Ma San showed the letter once more; the steward looked at the letter, glanced toward the main hall, said nothing, and let him into the line — how to make it up, the steward decides.

The third trial tested nerve, in an old forest west outside the gate. Each tree older and darker than the last; walking in at noon was like walking into dusk. In the middle stood an old pine, and under it, on an iron chain thicker than a man's leg, was chained a demon beast: body like a fox's but bigger than an ox; nine heads, nine tails, and four tiger's claws. The nine heads all turned to stare at every child who walked into the forest; the nine mouths opened together, and its cry was like nine infants wailing at once, knocking about the forest till your scalp crawled and your feet went soft.

The forest was kept by another steward, who stood at its edge. "Chained in there is a Longzhi; it's been chained a few decades. Go in, walk to the foot of the old pine, touch the bark, come out, and you get a stroke. One at a time." The first child to go in walked fewer than ten steps and ran out crying. The second walked five. The third stood at the edge, legs trembling a long time, never took a step, and was dragged off through the crowd by his father.

While they queued, a boy in a silk jacket — his family had hired a tutor — seeing everyone afraid, decided to show off, wagged his head and began reciting the *Classic of Mountains and Seas*: "There is a beast there, shaped like a fox, with nine tails, nine heads and tiger's claws; its name is the Longzhi; its voice is like an infant's —" There he stopped. A child beside him asked, "Its voice is like an infant's, and then?" The boy in silk slowly went white, his lips trembled twice, and then he squeezed out the last three words: "…it… eats… people." Dead silence all round. A moment later somebody went *waaah*, and then they were all crying.

Ma Xiaobao went in. He took three steps. As the third step landed, all nine of the Longzhi's heads turned toward him. Ma Xiaobao stopped and didn't move, and after a while everyone outside the forest could see, under the legs of his silk trousers, a puddle slowly spreading. Two servants rushed in and carried him out between them, one on each side. Hoisted in mid-air, legs kicking, he was still shouting: "I didn't! It's dew! It's dew!" This time nobody outside the forest could hold it in. "Hahahaha!" They laughed till they reeled, some squatting with their arms round their bellies, some thumping the backs of whoever stood beside them. Only one man didn't laugh: Ma San.

But Ma San didn't leave. He stood in the crowd, and his eyes moved off his son's wet trousers, inch by inch, until they came to rest on Xiaoman at the back of the queue. He beckoned Ge Liu over and said a few words low. Ge Liu's face changed; he shook his head. Ma San said something more and took a silver ingot from his coat. Ge Liu looked at the ingot a long time and didn't take it. Ma San's face darkened. "Then you can forget the five taels too." Ge Liu said nothing and stepped back to the rear of the crowd — but he didn't leave. Ma San pushed the ingot into the hand of a servant beside him, then took out a smaller piece, walked to the forest's edge, and slipped it into the sleeve of the steward who kept the forest.

Before Xiaoman's turn he waited outside the forest the better part of two hours. The other children, while they waited, cried, or shut their eyes and chanted to the Buddha. Xiaoman did nothing. He squatted at the edge of the trees, head on one side, and listened. He saw the servant with the silver too: squeezed to the very front of the crowd, feeling on the ground for a pebble, weighing it, feeling for another, choosing the roundest and holding it in his fist, his eyes never leaving Xiaoman. Xiaoman understood — that pebble was meant for him. Inside the forest, standing with his back to the crowd, the pebble could only hit his back. Only once did he look up: Ah He walked into the forest with her eyes shut, step by step, not fast, not slow, reached the foot of the pine, touched the bark, and walked out again with her eyes shut; from first to last she never looked at the beast.

Shidan was queued behind him, and squatted down next to him. There was only one stroke on his tag; even if he passed the third trial he couldn't fill three, but he queued all the same. He said quietly, "You could work it out." Xiaoman said, "What?" Shidan said, "Those nine numbers. You can work things out, and you can hear things." He rubbed his calloused hands on his knees again and again. "I can't fill three, but I'm going in to touch it anyway. Once I've touched it, at the testing I'll go and kneel and beg. That steward who nodded — he knows the people from Mount Taihua." Xiaoman opened his mouth and nothing came out.

His father had taught him how to tell a wolf's howl from the wind: a howl comes out of a chest, it's warm; the wind has only a hole, and however loud, it's hollow. He listened for two hours. Each time the nine heads cried, he listened. In the end he noticed something strange: each time the nine mouths opened together and nine cries poured out, the needles of the old pine deep in the forest trembled with only one of them. The other eight, however loud, never stirred a needle.

His turn came. He walked into the forest, didn't rush forward, stopped where the chain couldn't reach, stood still, and closed his eyes. The nine kinds of crying poured into his ears together. He listened to them one by one. The first was hollow, like wind blowing into a cracked jar. The second was hollow too, like someone shouting into a dry well and the well shouting back. The third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh — hollow. The ninth, hollow. Only the eighth was not. The eighth came out of a chest; between breaths it carried heat, a rankness he couldn't name, and a hunger. A very deep hunger, frantic, reckless, as if it could eat the whole forest, the whole mountain, and not be full. The other eight were all its shadows.

He had stood too long. At the edge of the forest the keeping steward glanced up at the sky; the sun was already slanting west and there were a hundred-odd still behind. He waved his hand: "Standing still doesn't count. Next — go in together, hurry it up." So Shidan came in too, stepping in Xiaoman's footprints, and stopped two paces behind him. "I'll follow you," he whispered.

Xiaoman opened his eyes, bent down, and picked up a stone.

label.en: Third trial · Hear the true head

exits.means: fights the Longzhi, takes the third trial

withdrawn.zh: 蠪侄缩回古松后面，九个头龇着牙。守林的执事：「再来。」
withdrawn.en: The Longzhi shrinks back behind the pine, nine heads baring their teeth. The forest steward: "Again."

story.zh:
就在这时，林子外头「嗖」的一声，一颗石子从人堆里飞进来，不偏不倚，打在蠪侄的后腿上。那兽吃了痛，九个脑袋一齐昂起，铁链「哗啦」一声绷得笔直，古松都给扯得晃了一晃，松根下的铁桩连泥拔起半尺，链子长出一截——它没有去扑那扔石子的人。它扑向了离它最近的那一个。小满算准了石子冲他来，没算到，它是冲那兽去的。

一只虎爪带着风，劈头盖脸地朝小满扫过来。便在这时，他胸口那块木牌忽然一烫，烫得他心口一跳，一个很小、很困、从极深极深的地方浮上来的声音，在他耳朵里道：

⟪「……左边。」⟫

爪子是从左边来的。他想也没想，往右一滚。那虎爪擦着他的左肩扫了过去，撕开了袄子，带走一层皮。他滚在地上，手里那块石头已经出手了——不偏不倚，正正地砸在第八个脑袋的鼻尖上。

蠪侄登时愣住了。它那一扑的势子，在半空里一滞，仿佛忽然忘了自己要做什么。然后，另外八个脑袋，一下子散了，像一口哈在冬天窗户上的热气，眨一眨眼，便什么都没有了。林子里只剩下一只狐狸模样的兽，一个脑袋，一条尾巴，比牛还大，缩回古松后面去了。

林子里忽然很静。

小满爬起来，回头。

那一爪，扫空了他，没有扫空。他身后两步远，石蛋躺在松针上，从左肩到右腰，三道口子，袄子、皮肉，一齐开了。他还睁着眼睛，看着林子顶上那一小块天，像是不明白自己怎么躺下了。

小满扑过去，两只手按在那三道口子上，按不住。血是热的，从他指头缝里往外冒，冒到松针上，松针一根一根都红了。石蛋的嘴动了动。小满把耳朵凑过去。

「……太华……多远？」

小满道：「不远。」

石蛋的眼睛在他脸上停了一停，像是信了，又像是没信。然后那双眼睛就不动了。他那一只手里，还攥着那块考牌，攥得死紧，牌子上一道，是他自己一级一级爬上来的。

小满跪在那里，手还按着。林子外头的人声，过了好一会儿才涌进他耳朵里来。

守林子的执事已经一把攥住了马家那个家丁的手腕，从他手心里抠出了第二颗石子。那家丁脸色煞白，道：「手、手滑……」马三挤上前来，往执事袖子里又塞了一样东西。执事掂了掂袖子，松了手，低头看了一眼林子里，翻开名册，提起笔，在一行字后头写了四个字：**林中自失。**又道：「一个一个进，是他自己跟进去的。」小满跪在松针上，心里只有一句：一块儿进，是他喊的。

人堆后头有人道：「石子是那家丁扔的。」是葛六。他从人堆后头一步一步走到前头来，红绸刀鞘挂在腰里，脸上一点酒色也没有，「三爷一锭银子，先找的我，我没接。我看见了。」四下里静了。马三笑道：「葛镖头喝多了。」执事看了看马三，又看了看葛六，把笔搁下，道：「名册写了，就是写了。」

小满跪在松针上，没有回头。他去掰石蛋攥着考牌的那只手，掰不开。

执事在林子口喊：「沈小满。松树皮没摸，不算过。」

他把石蛋背了起来。石蛋比他高半个头，背在背上，两只脚拖在地上，脚后跟在松针里犁出两道沟。他一步一步把他背出林子，放在林子口的草地上，拿自己撕破了的袄子盖住了那三道口子。然后他转过身，又走进林子，走过那只缩在古松后头、正舔着爪子的兽，伸手在松树皮上按了一下。手上的血，在树皮上留了一个印子。

沈小满走出林子，执事在他的考牌上画了第三道。三道画满了。

胸口的木牌凉凉的，凉得像从来没有热过。他没有说谢。
story.en:
Just then there was a *whizz* from outside the forest: a pebble flew in from the crowd and struck the Longzhi square on the hind leg. The beast, stung, reared all nine heads; the chain snapped taut with a *clang*, and even the old pine swayed; the iron stake at its roots tore half a foot up out of the mud, and the chain ran out a length longer — it didn't go for whoever threw the pebble. It went for the one nearest to it. Xiaoman had reckoned the pebble was meant for him; he hadn't reckoned it was meant for the beast.

A tiger's claw came sweeping at Xiaoman's head with a rush of wind. At that moment the token at his chest burned, a jolt to his heart, and a small, sleepy voice, as if rising from somewhere very, very deep, said in his ear:

⟪"…Left."⟫

The claw was coming from the left. Without a thought he rolled right. The tiger claw swept past his left shoulder, tore his jacket open and took a layer of skin. Rolling on the ground, he had already thrown the stone in his hand — dead true, smack on the tip of the eighth head's nose.

The Longzhi froze. Its pounce hung in mid-air a moment, as if it had suddenly forgotten what it meant to do. Then the other eight heads scattered all at once, like breath fogged on a winter window — a blink, and nothing. Left in the forest was one fox-like beast, one head, one tail, bigger than an ox, shrinking back behind the old pine.

The forest went suddenly quiet.

Xiaoman got up and turned round.

That swipe had missed him, and had not missed. Two paces behind him Shidan lay on the pine needles, three gashes from his left shoulder to his right hip, jacket and flesh opened together. His eyes were still open, looking at the small patch of sky above the trees, as if he couldn't understand how he came to be lying down.

Xiaoman threw himself down and pressed both hands on the three gashes; he couldn't hold them. The blood was hot and welled between his fingers onto the pine needles, and needle by needle they went red. Shidan's lips moved. Xiaoman put his ear close.

"…Taihua… how far?"

Xiaoman said, "Not far."

Shidan's eyes rested on his face a moment, as if he believed it, and as if he didn't. Then the eyes stopped moving. In one hand he still gripped his trial tag, gripped it hard; on it, one stroke, which he had climbed for himself, step by step.

Xiaoman knelt there, his hands still pressing. It was a long while before the voices outside the forest came back into his ears.

The keeping steward had already seized the Ma servant by the wrist and dug a second pebble out of his palm. The servant had gone white. "Sl-slipped…" Ma San pushed forward and slid something more into the steward's sleeve. The steward weighed the sleeve, let go, glanced into the forest, opened the register, took up his brush, and wrote four words after one line: **Lost himself in the forest.** He added, "One at a time — he followed in on his own." Xiaoman knelt on the needles with one thought: go in together — he was the one who called it.

From the back of the crowd someone said, "That servant threw the pebble." It was Ge Liu. He walked step by step from the back of the crowd to the front, the red-silk scabbard at his waist, not a trace of drink on his face. "The Third Master's ingot — he came to me first, and I wouldn't take it. I saw it." Silence all round. Ma San laughed. "Escort Ge has had a few." The steward looked at Ma San, then at Ge Liu, laid down the brush, and said, "The register's written. It's written."

Xiaoman knelt on the pine needles and didn't turn round. He tried to open Shidan's hand, the one gripping the trial tag. It wouldn't open.

The steward called from the forest's edge: "Shen Xiaoman. You haven't touched the bark — it doesn't count."

He lifted Shidan onto his back. Shidan was half a head taller; on his back, Shidan's feet dragged on the ground, his heels ploughing two furrows through the pine needles. Step by step he carried him out of the forest, laid him on the grass at its edge, and covered the three gashes with his own torn jacket. Then he turned, walked back into the forest, past the beast shrunk behind the old pine licking its claw, and pressed his hand once against the bark. The blood on his hand left a print on it.

Shen Xiaoman walked out of the forest, and the steward drew the third stroke on his tag. Three strokes, full.

The token on his chest was cold, as cold as if it had never been warm. He didn't say thank you.
